questions.question: Jobs arrive at a queue at epochs $A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$. For a time $t\geq0$, what quantity does the counting process value $A(t)$ give?
options: The time at which the $t$-th job arrives, read off from the epochs
The number of jobs present in the system at time $t$
The number of jobs that have arrived in the interval $[0,t]$
The time elapsed at $t$ since the most recent arrival

questions.question: Jobs arrive at ordered epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$, and $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ is their counting process. Which combination of properties does every sample path $t\mapsto A(t)$ have?
options: Integer-valued, strictly increasing and right-continuous in $t$

questions.question: Jobs arrive at ordered epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$, and $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ is their counting process. For an integer $k\geq1$ and a time $t\geq0$, the event $\{A(t)\geq k\}$ is the same as which event about the epochs?
options: The event $\{A_k<t\}$: job $k$ arrived strictly before $t$
The event $\{A_k\leq t\}$: job $k$ arrived at or before $t$
The event $\{A_k\geq t\}$: job $k$ arrives at or after $t$
The event $\{A_{k+1}\leq t\}$: a further job beyond job $k$ is already in

questions.question: Arrival epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$ define $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ and inter-arrival times $X_k=A_k-A_{k-1}$, $A_0=0$. If only the whole path $t\mapsto A(t)$ is recorded, what can be recovered?
options: Only the long-run arrival rate, since a path of counts carries no timing of single jobs
Only the number of arrivals in each interval, but not the epochs of individual jobs
The epochs and gaps only when the gaps are i.i.d. exponential, as in a Poisson process
Every epoch, via $A_k=\min\{t\colon A(t)\geq k\}$, and hence every gap $X_k$

questions.question: Jobs arrive at ordered epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$, and $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ is their counting process. The convention $A_0=0$ is also used. Which statement about the value $A(0)$ is correct?
options: $A(0)=0$ always, because the convention $A_0=0$ fixes the count at time $0$
$A(0)=0$ always, because arrivals at time $0$ fall outside the counted interval
$A(0)$ is the number of jobs with $A_k=0$, so it is $0$ only if none arrives at time $0$
$A(0)=1$ always, because the epoch $A_0=0$ satisfies $A_0\leq0$ and is counted

questions.question: Jobs arrive at epochs $A=(2,3,7,8,12)$ minutes, and $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$. What is $A(7)$?
Jobs arrive at epochs $A=(0.5,3,3.5,6,8,11)$, and $A(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$. Using $A(t)-A(s)$, how many jobs arrive in the interval $(3,8]$?

An arrival counting process satisfies $A(t)=0$ on $[0,2)$, $A(t)=1$ on $[2,3)$, $A(t)=2$ on $[3,6)$, $A(t)=3$ on $[6,10)$ and $A(t)=4$ for $t\geq10$. Using $A_k=\min\{t\colon A(t)\geq k\}$, what is the arrival epoch $A_3$?
Jobs arrive exactly every $3$ minutes, starting at time $3$, so $A_k=3k$ for $k=1,2,\ldots$. Which formula gives the counting process $A(t)$, the number of arrivals in $[0,t]$, for $t\geq0$?

Inter-arrival times of jobs are $X=(1.5,\,2,\,0.5,\,3,\,2.5,\,1)$ minutes, with $X_k=A_k-A_{k-1}$ and $A_0=0$. How many arrivals does the counting process give in $[0,6.5]$, that is, what is $A(6.5)$?

Jobs arrive at ordered epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$, and $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ is their counting process. For a time $t$ with $A(t)\geq1$, which statement about the epoch $A_{A(t)}$ is correct?
options: $A_{A(t)}=t$ for every $t$, since $A(\cdot)$ and $A_{\cdot}$ are inverse maps
$A_{A(t)}\geq t$: it is the epoch of the first arrival at or after $t$
$A_{A(t)}<t$ for every $t$: it is the last arrival strictly before $t$
$A_{A(t)}\leq t$: it is the epoch of the last arrival in $[0,t]$

questions.question: Jobs arrive at ordered epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$, and $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$ is their counting process. Job $k$ arrives at $A_k$ and no other job arrives at that epoch. Which pair gives the left limit $A(A_k-)$ and the value $A(A_k)$?
Jobs arrive at ordered epochs $0\leq A_1\leq A_2\leq\cdots$ with $A_k\to\infty$, and $A(t)$ is the number of arrivals in $[0,t]$. Which formula equals $A(t)$ for every $t\geq0$?
options: $\min\{k\colon A_k\geq t\}$, the index of the first job arriving at or after $t$
$\min\{k\colon A_k>t\}$, the index of the first job arriving after $t$
$\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$, the largest index whose epoch is at most $t$
$\max\{k\colon A_k<t\}$, the largest index whose epoch is before $t$

questions.question: A system starts empty, $L(0)=0$. Jobs arrive at $A=(1,3,6,8)$ and depart at $D=(2,6,9,10)$; $A(t)$ and $D(t)=\max\{k\colon D_k\leq t\}$ count arrivals and departures in $[0,t]$. Using $L(t)=A(t)-D(t)+L(0)$, what is $L(6)$?
Arrival epochs are $A_k=3k+\sqrt{k}$ minutes for $k=1,2,\ldots$. Find the long-run arrival rate $\lambda=\lim_{t\to\infty}A(t)/t$ of their counting process $A(t)$.
At a single first-come-first-served server, jobs arrive at $A=(0,1,4)$ and depart at $D=(3,5,6)$. With $A(t)$ the number of arrivals in $[0,t]$, the workload is $W(t)=[D_{A(t)}-t]^+$. What is $W(4)$?

Jobs arrive with i.i.d. inter-arrival times $X_k$, each uniformly distributed on $[0,2]$ minutes (mean $1$), and $A(t)$ counts the arrivals in $[0,t]$. Is $A(t)$ a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=1$ per minute?
options: Yes: a counting process with i.i.d. gaps of mean $1$ is Poisson with rate $1$
No: it is a counting process, but Poisson needs i.i.d. $\operatorname{Exp}(\lambda)$ gaps
No: it is not a counting process at all, since those require exponential gaps
Yes, approximately: the long-run rate is $1$, so it is Poisson for large $t$

questions.question: Epochs $A_k=1-\frac{1}{k+1}$, $k=1,2,\ldots$, are ordered but converge to $1$ instead of tending to $\infty$. What happens to $A(t)=\max\{k\colon A_k\leq t\}$, the count of epochs in $[0,t]$?
options: $A(t)$ is finite for every $t$, since each single epoch $A_k$ is a finite number
$A(t)=0$ for every $t\geq1$, since no job arrives after time $1$
$A(t)$ is finite for every $t$ but is no longer right-continuous at $t=1$
$A(t)$ is finite for $t<1$, but for $t\geq1$ infinitely many epochs lie in $[0,t]$

questions.question: An arrival counting process satisfies $A(t)=0$ on $[0,2)$, $A(t)=1$ on $[2,5)$, $A(t)=3$ on $[5,8)$ and $A(t)=4$ for $t\geq8$. With $A_k=\min\{t\colon A(t)\geq k\}$ and $X_k=A_k-A_{k-1}$, what is the inter-arrival time $X_3$?

Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=1$ per minute, so the count $A(t)$ of arrivals in $[0,t]$ is $\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda t)$. What is the probability $\mathbb{P}(A_2\leq2)$ that the second job has arrived by time $2$?
